sanskrit_iast:
tvayā pṛṣṭā jagattāta na lajjā kathituṃ mama ..
yeṣāṃ bhāraiḥ pīḍitā'haṃ śrūyatāṃ kathayāmi te .. 18 ..
meaning:
त्वया पृष्टा जगत्तात न लज्जा कथितुं मम ..
येषां भारैः पीडिताऽहं श्रूयतां कथयामि ते .. 18 ..

sanskrit_iast:
kṛṣṇabhaktivihīnā ye ye ca tadbhaktaniṃdakāḥ ..
teṣāṃ mahāpātakināmaśaktā bhāravāhane .. 19 ..
meaning:
कृष्णभक्तिविहीना ये ये च तद्भक्तनिंदकाः ..
तेषां महापातकिनामशक्ता भारवाहने .. 19 ..

sanskrit_iast:
svadharmācārahīnā ye nityakṛtyavivarjitāḥ ..
śraddhāhīnāśca vedeṣu teṣāṃ bhāreṇa pīḍitā .. 20 ..
meaning:
स्वधर्माचारहीना ये नित्यकृत्यविवर्जिताः ..
श्रद्धाहीनाश्च वेदेषु तेषां भारेण पीडिता .. 20 ..

sanskrit_iast:
pitṛmātṛgurustrīṇāṃ poṣaṇaṃ putrapoṣyayoḥ ..
ye na kurvaṃti teṣāṃ ca na śaktā bhāravāhane .. 21 ..
meaning:
पितृमातृगुरुस्त्रीणां पोषणं पुत्रपोष्ययोः ..
ये न कुर्वंति तेषां च न शक्ता भारवाहने .. 21 ..

sanskrit_iast:
ye mithyāvādinastāta dayāsatya vivarjitāḥ ..
niṃdakā gurudevānāṃ teṣāṃ bhāreṇa pīḍitā ..22..
meaning:
ये मिथ्यावादिनस्तात दयासत्य विवर्जिताः ..
निंदका गुरुदेवानां तेषां भारेण पीडिता ..22..

sanskrit_iast:
mitradrohī kṛtaghnaśca mithyāsākṣyapradāyakaḥ ..
viśvāsaghno nyāsahartā teṣāṃ bhāreṇa pīḍitā .. 23 ..
meaning:
मित्रद्रोही कृतघ्नश्च मिथ्यासाक्ष्यप्रदायकः ..
विश्वासघ्नो न्यासहर्ता तेषां भारेण पीडिता .. 23 ..

sanskrit_iast:
kalyāṇasūktasāmāni harernāmaikamaṃgalam ..
kurvaṃti vikrayaṃ ye vai teṣāṃ bhāreṇa pīḍitā .. 24 ..
meaning:
कल्याणसूक्तसामानि हरेर्नामैकमंगलम् ..
कुर्वंति विक्रयं ये वै तेषां भारेण पीडिता .. 24 ..

sanskrit_iast:
jīvaghātī gurudrohī grāmayājī ca lubdhakaḥ ..
śavadāhī śūdrabhojī teṣāṃ bhāreṇa pīḍitā .. 25 ..
meaning:
जीवघाती गुरुद्रोही ग्रामयाजी च लुब्धकः ..
शवदाही शूद्रभोजी तेषां भारेण पीडिता .. 25 ..

sanskrit_iast:
pūjāyajñopavāsādi vratāni vividhāni ca ..
ye ye mūḍhā vihaṃtārasteṣāṃ bhāreṇa pīḍitā ..26..
meaning:
पूजायज्ञोपवासादि व्रतानि विविधानि च ..
ये ये मूढा विहंतारस्तेषां भारेण पीडिता ..26..

sanskrit_iast:
sadā dviṣaṃti ye pāpā goviprasuravaiṣṇavān ..
hariṃ harikathāṃ bhaktiṃ teṣāṃ bhāreṇa pīḍitā .. 27 ..
meaning:
सदा द्विषंति ये पापा गोविप्रसुरवैष्णवान् ..
हरिं हरिकथां भक्तिं तेषां भारेण पीडिता .. 27 ..

sanskrit_iast:
śaṃkhādīnāṃ ca bhāreṇa pīḍitā'haṃ yathā vidhe ..
tato'dhikānāṃ daityānāṃ bhāreṇa paripīḍitā ..28..
meaning:
शंखादीनां च भारेण पीडिताऽहं यथा विधे ..
ततोऽधिकानां दैत्यानां भारेण परिपीडिता ..28..

sanskrit_iast:
ityevaṃ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ madvyathāyā nivedanam ..
tvayā yadi supālyā'haṃ pratīkāraṃ kuru prabho..29..
meaning:
इत्येवं कथितं सर्वं मद्व्यथाया निवेदनम् ..
त्वया यदि सुपाल्याऽहं प्रतीकारं कुरु प्रभो..29..

sanskrit_iast:
ityevamuktvā vasudhā ruroda ca muhurmuhuḥ ..
brahmā tadrodanaṃ dṛṣṭvā tāmuvāca kṛpānidhiḥ .. 30 ..
meaning:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा वसुधा रुरोद च मुहुर्मुहुः ..
ब्रह्मा तद्रोदनं दृष्ट्वा तामुवाच कृपानिधिः .. 30 ..

sanskrit_iast:
bhāraṃ tavāpaneṣyāmi dasyūnāmapyupāyataḥ ..
upāyato'pi kāryāṇi siddhyaṃtyeva vasundhare ..31..
meaning:
भारं तवापनेष्यामि दस्यूनामप्युपायतः ..
उपायतोऽपि कार्याणि सिद्ध्यंत्येव वसुन्धरे ..31..

sanskrit_iast:
kālena bhāraharaṇaṃ kariṣyati madīśvaraḥ ..
mantraṃ maṃgalakumbhaṃ ca śivaliṃgaṃ ca kuṃkumam .. 32 ..
meaning:
कालेन भारहरणं करिष्यति मदीश्वरः ..
मन्त्रं मंगलकुम्भं च शिवलिंगं च कुंकुमम् .. 32 ..

sanskrit_iast:
madhukāṣṭhaṃ caṃdanaṃ ca kastūrīṃ tīrthamṛttikām ..
khaṅgagaṃḍakakhaṃḍaṃ ca sphāṭikaṃ padmarāgakam ..33..
meaning:
मधुकाष्ठं चंदनं च कस्तूरीं तीर्थमृत्तिकाम् ..
खङ्गगंडकखंडं च स्फाटिकं पद्मरागकम् ..33..

sanskrit_iast:
iṃdranīlaṃ sūryamaṇiṃ rudrākṣaṃ kuśamūlakam ..
śālagrāmaśilāṃ śaṃkhaṃ tulasīṃ pratimāṃ jalam ..34..
meaning:
इंद्रनीलं सूर्यमणिं रुद्राक्षं कुशमूलकम् ..
शालग्रामशिलां शंखं तुलसीं प्रतिमां जलम् ..34..

sanskrit_iast:
śaṃkhaṃ pradīpamālāṃ ca śilāmarcyāṃ ca ghaṃṭikām..
nirmālyaṃ caiva naivedyaṃ haridvarṇamaṇiṃ tathā..
graṃthiyuktaṃ yajñasūtraṃ darpaṇaṃ śvetacāmaram ..35..
meaning:
शंखं प्रदीपमालां च शिलामर्च्यां च घंटिकाम्..
निर्माल्यं चैव नैवेद्यं हरिद्वर्णमणिं तथा..
ग्रंथियुक्तं यज्ञसूत्रं दर्पणं श्वेतचामरम् ..35..

sanskrit_iast:
gorocanaṃ ca muktāṃ ca śuktiṃ māṇikyameva ca ..
purāṇasaṃhitāṃ vahniṃ karpūraṃ paraśuṃ tathā .. 36 ..
meaning:
गोरोचनं च मुक्तां च शुक्तिं माणिक्यमेव च ..
पुराणसंहितां वह्निं कर्पूरं परशुं तथा .. 36 ..

sanskrit_iast:
rajataṃ kāṃcanaṃ caiva pravālaṃ ratnameva ca ..
kuśabījaṃ tīrthatoyaṃ gavyaṃ gomūtragomayam .. 37 ..
meaning:
रजतं कांचनं चैव प्रवालं रत्नमेव च ..
कुशबीजं तीर्थतोयं गव्यं गोमूत्रगोमयम् .. 37 ..

sanskrit_iast:
tvayi ye sthāpayiṣyaṃti mūḍhāścaitāni sundari ..
pacyante kālasūtreṇa varṣāṇāmayutaṃ dhruvam ..38..
meaning:
त्वयि ये स्थापयिष्यंति मूढाश्चैतानि सुन्दरि ..
पच्यन्ते कालसूत्रेण वर्षाणामयुतं ध्रुवम् ..38..

sanskrit_iast:
brahmā pṛthvīṃ samāśvāsya devatābhistayā saha ..
jagāma jagatāṃ dhātā kailāsaṃ śaṃkarālayam .. 39 ..
meaning:
ब्रह्मा पृथ्वीं समाश्वास्य देवताभिस्तया सह ..
जगाम जगतां धाता कैलासं शंकरालयम् .. 39 ..

sanskrit_iast:
gatvā tamāśramaṃ ramyaṃ dadarśa śaṃkaraṃ vidhiḥ ..
vasaṃtamakṣayavaṭamūle svaḥsaritastaṭe.. 40 ..
meaning:
गत्वा तमाश्रमं रम्यं ददर्श शंकरं विधिः ..
वसंतमक्षयवटमूले स्वःसरितस्तटे.. 40 ..

sanskrit_iast:
vyāghracarmaparīdhānaṃ dakṣakanyāsthibhūṣaṇam ..
triśūlapaṭṭiśadharaṃ paṃcavaktraṃ trilocanam .. 41 ..
meaning:
व्याघ्रचर्मपरीधानं दक्षकन्यास्थिभूषणम् ..
त्रिशूलपट्टिशधरं पंचवक्त्रं त्रिलोचनम् .. 41 ..

sanskrit_iast:
nānāsiddhaiḥ parivṛtaṃ yogīṃdragaṇasevitam..
parito'psarasāṃ nṛtyaṃ paśyaṃtaṃ sasmitaṃ mudā .. 42 ..
meaning:
नानासिद्धैः परिवृतं योगींद्रगणसेवितम्..
परितोऽप्सरसां नृत्यं पश्यंतं सस्मितं मुदा .. 42 ..

even more so am I thoroughly oppressed by the burden of the Daityas. / Thus everything, the declaration of my anguish, has been told. / If I am to be well protected by you, O Lord, make a remedy." / Having spoken thus, the Earth wept again and again. / Seeing her weeping, Brahmā, an ocean of mercy, said to her: / "By appropriate means I shall remove your burden, even that of the robbers; / indeed, by appropriate means tasks are accomplished, O Earth. / In time, my Lord will accomplish the removal of the burden. / A mantra, an auspicious water-pot, a Śiva-liṅga, saffron, / madhuka-wood, sandalwood, musk, soil from sacred bathing-places, / a rhinoceros horn, crystal, ruby, / sapphire, sun-stone, rudrākṣa, kuśa-root, / a Śālagrāma stone, a conch, a tulasī plant, an image, water, / a conch, a row of lamps, a stone for worship, a bell, / offerings of flowers, food offerings, an emerald, / a sacred thread with its knot, a mirror, a white fly-whisk, / gorocana, pearl, mother-of-pearl, ruby, / a Purāṇa compendium, fire, camphor, an axe, / silver, gold, coral, and gems, / kuśa seed, water from sacred places, products of the cow, cow urine, and cow dung— / those fools who place these upon you, O beautiful lady, / are roasted by the Kālasūtra for ten thousand years without fail." / Having consoled the Earth, the Creator of the worlds, accompanied by her / and the gods, went to Kailāsa, the abode of Śaṅkara. / Having arrived at that delightful hermitage, the Creator saw Śaṅkara / dwelling at the base of the imperishable banyan tree on the bank of the heavenly river, / wearing a tiger skin, adorned with bones of Dakṣa's daughter, / holding a trident and a spear, five-faced, three-eyed, / surrounded by various Siddhas, served by the hosts of lordly yogins,
watching with a smile and with joy the dance of apsarases all around, / listening with curiosity to the music of the gandharvas, / looking with side-glances at Pārvatī who was gazing [at him] with love, / chanting with his five faces the solely auspicious name of Hari, / with horripilation, with a rosary of lotus seeds from the Mandākinī. / At that moment Brahmā stood before Dhūrjaṭi, / accompanied by the Earth and the hosts of gods, with their necks bowed. / Seeing the Guru of the universe, Śaṅkara swiftly stood up with devotion, / bowed with his head out of love, and then received his blessing. / All the deities bowed to Śaṅkara, whose crest is the moon; / the Earth bowed with devotion, and Hara bestowed a blessing. / Prajāpati related the matter to Pārvatī's lord; / having heard it, Śaṅkara, who is affectionate to his devotees, bowed his head at once. / Having heard of the peril to the devotee, Pārvatī and the Supreme Lord / became afflicted with grief; the Creator comforted them both. / Then Brahmā and Maheśa, having diligently consoled / the hosts of gods and the Earth, sent them home. / Then, having come quickly with the lord of the gods to the abode of Dharma, / and having deliberated with him, they went to the abode of Hari— / to Vaikuṇṭha, the supreme abode, the ultimate remover of old age and death, / sustained by the wind, the supreme realm above the cosmic egg, / ten million leagues above Brahmaloka, eternal, / indescribable by poets, wondrous, fashioned of jewels, / adorned with royal roads made of rubies and sapphires. / Travelling at the speed of thought, they all reached that enchanting [place]; / having gone to the inner chamber of Hari, the gods saw Śrī Hari, / seated on a jewelled throne, adorned with jewelled ornaments, / embellished with jewelled armlets, bracelets, and jewelled anklets, / his cheeks radiant with a pair of jewelled earrings,

sanskrit_iast:
gaṃdharvāṇāṃ ca saṃgītaṃ śrutavaṃtaṃ kutūhalāt ..
paśyaṃtīṃ pārvatīṃ prītyā paśyaṃtaṃ vakracakṣuṣā .. 43 ..
meaning:
गंधर्वाणां च संगीतं श्रुतवंतं कुतूहलात् ..
पश्यंतीं पार्वतीं प्रीत्या पश्यंतं वक्रचक्षुषा .. 43 ..

sanskrit_iast:
japaṃtaṃ pañcavaktreṇa harernāmaikamaṅgalam ..
maṃdākinīpadmabījamālayā pulakāṃkitam .. 44..
meaning:
जपंतं पञ्चवक्त्रेण हरेर्नामैकमङ्गलम् ..
मंदाकिनीपद्मबीजमालया पुलकांकितम् .. 44..

sanskrit_iast:
etasminnaṃtare brahmā tasthāvagre sa dhūrjaṭeḥ ..
pṛthivyā surasaṃghaiśca sārddhaṃ praṇatakaṃdharaiḥ .. 45 ..
meaning:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे ब्रह्मा तस्थावग्रे स धूर्जटेः ..
पृथिव्या सुरसंघैश्च सार्द्धं प्रणतकंधरैः .. 45 ..

sanskrit_iast:
uttasthau śaṃkaraḥ śīghraṃ bhaktyā dṛṣṭvā jagadgurum ..
nanāma mūrdhnā saṃprītyā labdhavānāśiṣaṃ tataḥ .. 46 ..
meaning:
उत्तस्थौ शंकरः शीघ्रं भक्त्या दृष्ट्वा जगद्गुरुम् ..
ननाम मूर्ध्ना संप्रीत्या लब्धवानाशिषं ततः .. 46 ..

sanskrit_iast:
praṇemurdevatāḥ sarve śaṃkaraṃ caṃdraśekharam ..
praṇanāma dharā bhaktyā cāśiṣaṃ yuyuje haraḥ .. 47 ..
meaning:
प्रणेमुर्देवताः सर्वे शंकरं चंद्रशेखरम् ..
प्रणनाम धरा भक्त्या चाशिषं युयुजे हरः .. 47 ..

sanskrit_iast:
vṛttāṃtaṃ kathayāmāsa pārvatīśaṃ prajāpatiḥ ..
śrutvā natamukhastūrṇaṃ śaṃkaro bhaktavatsalaḥ .. 48 ..
meaning:
वृत्तांतं कथयामास पार्वतीशं प्रजापतिः ..
श्रुत्वा नतमुखस्तूर्णं शंकरो भक्तवत्सलः .. 48 ..

sanskrit_iast:
bhaktāpāyaṃ samākarṇya pārvatīparameśvarau ..
babhūvatustau duḥkhārtau bodhayāmāsa tau vidhiḥ .. 49 ..
meaning:
भक्तापायं समाकर्ण्य पार्वतीपरमेश्वरौ ..
बभूवतुस्तौ दुःखार्तौ बोधयामास तौ विधिः .. 49 ..

sanskrit_iast:
tato brahmā maheśaśca surasaṃghānvasuṃdharām ..
gṛhaṃ prasthāpayāmāsa samāśvāsya prayatnataḥ ..50..
meaning:
ततो ब्रह्मा महेशश्च सुरसंघान्वसुंधराम् ..
गृहं प्रस्थापयामास समाश्वास्य प्रयत्नतः ..50..

sanskrit_iast:
tato deveśvaraistūrṇamāgatya dharmamaṃdiram ..
saha tena samālocya prajagmurbhavanaṃ hareḥ .. 51 ..
meaning:
ततो देवेश्वरैस्तूर्णमागत्य धर्ममंदिरम् ..
सह तेन समालोच्य प्रजग्मुर्भवनं हरेः .. 51 ..

sanskrit_iast:
vaikuṃṭhaṃ paramaṃ dhāma jarāmṛtyuharaṃ param ..
vāyunā dhāryamāṇaṃ ca brahmāṃḍādūrdhvamuttamam ..
koṭiyojanamūrdhvaṃ ca brahmalokātsanātanam 52 ..
meaning:
वैकुंठं परमं धाम जरामृत्युहरं परम् ..
वायुना धार्यमाणं च ब्रह्मांडादूर्ध्वमुत्तमम् ..
कोटियोजनमूर्ध्वं च ब्रह्मलोकात्सनातनम् 52 ..

sanskrit_iast:
varṇanīyaṃ na kavibhirvicitraṃ ratnanirmitam ..
padmarāgairiṃdranīlai rājamārgairvibhūṣitam .. 53 ..
meaning:
वर्णनीयं न कविभिर्विचित्रं रत्ननिर्मितम् ..
पद्मरागैरिंद्रनीलै राजमार्गैर्विभूषितम् .. 53 ..

sanskrit_iast:
te manoyāyinaḥ sarve saṃprāpustaṃ manoharam ..
hareraṃtaḥpuraṃ gatvā dadṛśuḥ śrīhariṃ surāḥ .. 54 ..
meaning:
ते मनोयायिनः सर्वे संप्रापुस्तं मनोहरम् ..
हरेरंतःपुरं गत्वा ददृशुः श्रीहरिं सुराः .. 54 ..

sanskrit_iast:
ratnasiṃhāsanasthaṃ ca ratnālaṃkārabhūṣitam ..
ratnakeyūravalayaratnanūpuraśobhitam .. 95 ..
meaning:
रत्नसिंहासनस्थं च रत्नालंकारभूषितम् ..
रत्नकेयूरवलयरत्ननूपुरशोभितम् .. 95 ..

sanskrit_iast:
ratnakuṇḍalayugmena gaṃḍasthalavirājitam ..
pītavastraparīdhānaṃ vanamālāvibhūṣitam .. 56 ..
meaning:
रत्नकुण्डलयुग्मेन गंडस्थलविराजितम् ..
पीतवस्त्रपरीधानं वनमालाविभूषितम् .. 56 ..

sanskrit_iast:
śāṃtaṃ sarasvatīkāṃtaṃ lakṣmīdhṛtapadāṃbujam ..
koṭikaṃdarpalīlābhaṃ smitavaktraṃ caturbhujam .. 57 ..
meaning:
शांतं सरस्वतीकांतं लक्ष्मीधृतपदांबुजम् ..
कोटिकंदर्पलीलाभं स्मितवक्त्रं चतुर्भुजम् .. 57 ..

sanskrit_iast:
sunaṃdanaṃdakumudaiḥ pārṣadairupasevitam ..
caṃdanokṣitasarvāṃgaṃ suratnamukuṭojjvalam ..
paramānaṃdarūpaṃ ca bhaktānugrahakārakam .. 58 ..
meaning:
सुनंदनंदकुमुदैः पार्षदैरुपसेवितम् ..
चंदनोक्षितसर्वांगं सुरत्नमुकुटोज्ज्वलम् ..
परमानंदरूपं च भक्तानुग्रहकारकम् .. 58 ..

sanskrit_iast:
taṃ praṇemuḥ sureṃdrāśca bhaktyā brahmādayo mune ..

text_mt:
Clothed in yellow garments, adorned with a garland of forest flowers,
peaceful, the beloved of Sarasvatī, his lotus feet held by Lakṣmī,
shining with the charm of millions of Kāmadevas, smiling-faced, four-armed,
attended upon by attendants such as Sunanda, Nanda, and Kumuda,
his entire body anointed with sandalwood paste, resplendent with an excellent crown of gems,
of the nature of supreme bliss, and bestowing grace upon his devotees —
to him the chiefs of the gods, Brahmā and the others, bowed down with devotion, O sage;
they praised him with supreme devotion, their necks bent in devotion,
overcome by the weight of supreme bliss, their bodies bristling with hair standing on end.
Brahmā said:
I bow down to the beloved of Kamalā, the peaceful, the desired object of all, Acyuta,
of whom we are distinct parts, while the gods are a fraction of a portion of a part;
and the Manus, the best of sages, human beings, and moving and unmoving creatures,
are produced from you, O immaculate one, as a fraction of a portion of a part of a part.
Śaṅkara said:
You are imperishable or immutable, manifest, unmanifest, the sovereign Lord,
beginningless, the source of all, consisting of bliss, having all forms,
the cause of the yogic powers beginning with atomicity, the cause of all causes,
knower of yogic powers, giver of yogic powers, of the nature of yogic power: who is able to praise you?
Dharma said:
A subject established in the Veda should be described by the wise;
who is capable of describing that which is beyond description in the Veda?
Whatever immaculate form of attributes is to be attributed to him —
beyond that, how can I praise him who is without gunas?
This hymn of praise of Brahmā and the others, uttered in six verses, O great sage,
having recited it, a person is freed from distress and obtains what is desired.
Having heard the hymn of praise of the gods, Hari himself said to them:
"Go you to Goloka, and I will go afterwards along with Śrī.
Those two, Nara and Nārāyaṇa, the dwellers in Śvetadvīpa,
these shall go to Goloka, and likewise goddess Sarasvatī;
Ananta, my Māyā, Kārttikeya, the leader of the Gaṇas,
and Sāvitrī the mother of the Vedas shall surely go afterwards.

sanskrit_iast:

meaning:

sanskrit_iast:
nārāyaṇaśca kṛṣṇo'haṃ śvetadvīpanivāsakṛt ..

meaning:

sanskrit_iast:

sanskrit_iast:
vayaṃ paścādgamiṣyāmaḥ sarveṣāmiṣṭasiddhaye ..
ityuktvā vai sabhāmadhye virarāma hariḥ svayam .. 72 ..
meaning:
वयं पश्चाद्गमिष्यामः सर्वेषामिष्टसिद्धये ..
इत्युक्त्वा वै सभामध्ये विरराम हरिः स्वयम् .. 72 ..

sanskrit_iast:
praṇamya devatāḥ sarvā jagmurgolokamadbhutam ..
vicitraṃ paramaṃ dhāma jarāmṛtyuharaṃ param .. 73 ..
meaning:
प्रणम्य देवताः सर्वा जग्मुर्गोलोकमद्भुतम् ..
विचित्रं परमं धाम जरामृत्युहरं परम् .. 73 ..

sanskrit_iast:

sanskrit_iast:
tamanirvacanīyaṃ ca devāste gamanotsukāḥ ..

sanskrit_iast:
dṛṣṭvā devāḥ sarittīraṃ vismayaṃ paramaṃ yayuḥ ..

meaning:
दृष्ट्वा देवाः सरित्तीरं विस्मयं परमं ययुः ..

sanskrit_iast:

sanskrit_iast:

sanskrit_iast:

meaning:
विधेरदृश्यामाश्चर्य निधिश्रेष्ठाकरान्वितम् ..

sanskrit_iast:

sanskrit_iast:

sanskrit_iast:

sanskrit_iast:

meaning:
दृष्ट्वा तु परमाश्चर्यं जग्मुस्तत्पारमीश्वराः ..

sanskrit_iast:

kalpavṛkṣaiḥ parivṛtaṃ veṣṭitaṃ kāmadhenubhiḥ .. 84 ..
meaning:
पारिजाततरूणां च वनराजिविराजितम् ..
कल्पवृक्षैः परिवृतं वेष्टितं कामधेनुभिः .. 84 ..
text_mt:
adorned with rows of forests of pārijāta trees,
surrounded by wish-fulfilling trees, encircled by kāmadhenus,
a crore of yojanas high, and in length ten times greater,
and measuring fifty crores of yojanas in the mountain's breadth.
Having the shape of a rampart, on its summit was the circular dance-ground,
ten yojanas wide, circular in shape, and sublime,
filled with a thousand flowering, fragrant flower gardens,
crowded with swarms of bees buzzing about;
adorned with chambers of love containing articles for amorous delight,
accompanied by thousands of crores of jeweled pavilions,
endowed with stairways of gems and jars of fine jewels,
beautified by pillars of emeralds,
studded all around with gems of the color of red lead,
and decorated with charming sapphires placed in their center;
resplendent with various gems, provided with ramparts of jewels,
and graced with four gateways equipped with door leaves;
provided with shoots of mango trees tied with ropes,
and surrounded on all sides by clusters of plantain trunks;
supplied with white grain, foliage, fruits, and sprouts of dūrvā grass,
and smeared with the essence of sandalwood, agallochum, musk, and saffron;
surrounded, O sage, by crores of groups of cowherd maidens
adorned with gem-ornaments, resplendent with garlands of jewels,
adorned with bracelets, armlets, and anklets made of gems,
with their cheek areas shining with pairs of jeweled earrings,
the fingers of their hands graceful and bright with jeweled rings,
the toes of their feet adorned with clusters of jeweled toe-rings,
adorned with jeweled ornaments, radiant with crowns of fine gems,
shining on the bridge of their noses with ornaments of pearls from noble elephants,
resplendent below their forelocks along with a dot of red lead,
having the lovely hue of campaka flowers, smeared with the fluid of sandalwood,
clothed in yellow garments, their bimba-fruit lips delightful.

sanskrit_iast:

sanskrit_iast:

meaning:

sanskrit_iast:

sanskrit_iast:

sanskrit_iast:

sanskrit_iast:

sanskrit_iast:

sanskrit_iast:

sanskrit_iast:

meaning:
वेष्टितं गोपकन्यानां समूहैः कोटिशो मुने ..

sanskrit_iast:

sanskrit_iast:

meaning:

sanskrit_iast:

meaning:

sanskrit_iast:

meaning:

sanskrit_iast:

meaning:
पीतवस्त्रपरीधानैर्बिंबाधरमनोहरैः ..
शरत्पार्वणचंद्राणां प्रभां मुष्णन्मुखोज्ज्वलैः .. 99 ..
text_mt: [Guarded] by groups of beautiful women whose faces steal the radiance of full autumn moons, / whose eyes rob the splendor of blossoming autumn lotuses, / adorned with musk leaf-drawings and radiant with lines of collyrium, / their braided hair adorned with garlands of blooming jasmine, / crowded with swarms of bees greedy for nectar, / humiliating elephants and wagtails by their graceful gait alone, / endowed with delicate smiles joined with arched eyebrows, / graced by rows of teeth resembling ripe pomegranate seeds, / decorated with elevated noses possessing the beauty of the bird-king's beak, / bowed as if by the weight of breasts resembling a pair of princely elephants' frontal lobes, / bowed under the heavy burden of plump hips and firm buttocks, / their minds shattered by the assaults of the arrows of love, / eager to gaze upon the beauty of their full-moon-like faces in mirrors, / their desires intent on serving Rādhikā's lotus feet; / guarded by command of Rādhikā, / and surrounded by hundreds of thousands of pleasure lakes, / surrounded and adorned with white and red lotuses, / always resounding with sweetly cooing swarms of bees, / furnished with thousands of blossoming, fragrant flower gardens, / and with crores of bower-cottages provided with flower-beds, / stocked with luxury articles, camphor-scented betel, and fine garments, / surrounded on all sides by jewel-lamps, white fly-whisks, and mirrors, / and adorned, O sage, with charming garlands of manifold flowers. / Having seen that rāsa pavilion, they came out of the mountain. / Then the discerning [gods] beheld a delightful and beautiful forest, / a forest named Vṛndāvana, beloved of Rādhā and Mādhava, / the pleasure-ground of the two, filled with groves of wish-granting trees, / stirred by gentle breezes moist with water from the banks of the Virajā, / made fragrant by cascades of flowers and lotus petals marked with musk,

sanskrit_iast:
śaratpraphullapadmānāṃ śobhāmoṣaṇalocanaiḥ ..
kastūrīpātrikāyuktai rekhāktakajjalojjvalaiḥ .. 100 ..
meaning:
शरत्प्रफुल्लपद्मानां शोभामोषणलोचनैः ..
कस्तूरीपात्रिकायुक्तै रेखाक्तकज्जलोज्ज्वलैः .. 100 ..

sanskrit_iast:
praphullamālatīmālājālaiḥkabaraśobhitaiḥ ..
madhulubdhamadhughrāṇāṃ samūhaiścāpi saṃkulaiḥ ..
cāruṇā gamanenaiva gajakhaṃjanagaṃjanaiḥ .. 101 ..
meaning:
प्रफुल्लमालतीमालाजालैःकबरशोभितैः ..
मधुलुब्धमधुघ्राणां समूहैश्चापि संकुलैः ..
चारुणा गमनेनैव गजखंजनगंजनैः .. 101 ..

sanskrit_iast:
vakrabhrūbhaṃgasaṃyogaślakṣṇasmitasamanvitaiḥ ..
pakvadāḍimabījābhadaṃtapaṃktivirājitaiḥ .. 102 ..
meaning:
वक्रभ्रूभंगसंयोगश्लक्ष्णस्मितसमन्वितैः ..
पक्वदाडिमबीजाभदंतपंक्तिविराजितैः .. 102 ..

sanskrit_iast:
khageṃdracaṃcuśobhāḍhyanāsikonnatabhūṣitaiḥ ..
gajeṃdragaṃḍayugmābhastanabhāranatairiva .. 103 ..
meaning:
खगेंद्रचंचुशोभाढ्यनासिकोन्नतभूषितैः ..
गजेंद्रगंडयुग्माभस्तनभारनतैरिव .. 103 ..

sanskrit_iast:
nitambakaṭhinaśroṇīpīnabhārabharānataiḥ ..
kaṃdarpaśaraceṣṭābhirjarjarībhūtamānasai .. 104 ..
meaning:
नितम्बकठिनश्रोणीपीनभारभरानतैः ..
कंदर्पशरचेष्टाभिर्जर्जरीभूतमानसै .. 104 ..

sanskrit_iast:
darpaṇaiḥ pūrṇacaṃdrāsyasauṃdaryadarśanotsukaiḥ ..
rādhikācaraṇāṃbhojasevāsaktamanorathaiḥ ..105..
meaning:
दर्पणैः पूर्णचंद्रास्यसौंदर्यदर्शनोत्सुकैः ..
राधिकाचरणांभोजसेवासक्तमनोरथैः ..105..

sanskrit_iast:
suṃdarīṇāṃ samūhaiśca rakṣitaṃ rādhikājñayā ..
krīḍāsarovarāṇāṃ ca lakṣaiśca pariveṣṭitam .. 106 ..
meaning:
सुंदरीणां समूहैश्च रक्षितं राधिकाज्ञया ..
क्रीडासरोवराणां च लक्षैश्च परिवेष्टितम् .. 106 ..

sanskrit_iast:
śvetaraktairlohitaiśca veṣṭitaiḥ padmarājitaiḥ ..
sukūjadbhirmadhughrāṇāṃ samūhaiḥ saṃkulaiḥ sadā .. 107 ..
meaning:
श्वेतरक्तैर्लोहितैश्च वेष्टितैः पद्मराजितैः ..
सुकूजद्भिर्मधुघ्राणां समूहैः संकुलैः सदा .. 107 ..

sanskrit_iast:
puṣpodyānasahasreṇa puṣpitena samanvitam ..
koṭikuṃjakuṭīraiśca puṣpaśayyāsamanvitaiḥ .. 106 ..
meaning:
पुष्पोद्यानसहस्रेण पुष्पितेन समन्वितम् ..
कोटिकुंजकुटीरैश्च पुष्पशय्यासमन्वितैः .. 106 ..

sanskrit_iast:
bhogadravyasakarpūratāṃbūlavastrasaṃyutaiḥ ..
ratnapradīpaiḥ paritaḥ śvetacāmaradarpaṇaiḥ .. .. 109 ..
meaning:
भोगद्रव्यसकर्पूरतांबूलवस्त्रसंयुतैः ..
रत्नप्रदीपैः परितः श्वेतचामरदर्पणैः .. .. 109 ..

sanskrit_iast:
vicitrapuṣpamālābhiḥ śobhitaiḥ śobhitaṃ mune ..
taṃ rāsamaṃḍapaṃ dṛṣṭvā jagmuste parvatādbahiḥ .. 110 ..
meaning:
विचित्रपुष्पमालाभिः शोभितैः शोभितं मुने ..
तं रासमंडपं दृष्ट्वा जग्मुस्ते पर्वताद्बहिः .. 110 ..

sanskrit_iast:
tato vicakṣaṇaṃ ramyaṃ dadṛśuḥ suṃdaraṃ vanam ..
vanaṃ vṛdāvanaṃ nāma rādhāmādhavayoḥ priyam .. 111 ..
meaning:
ततो विचक्षणं रम्यं ददृशुः सुंदरं वनम् ..
वनं वृदावनं नाम राधामाधवयोः प्रियम् .. 111 ..

sanskrit_iast:
krīḍāsthānaṃ tayoreva kalpavṛkṣacayānvitam ..
virajātīranīrāktaiḥ kaṃpitaṃ maṃdavāyubhiḥ .. 112 ..
meaning:
क्रीडास्थानं तयोरेव कल्पवृक्षचयान्वितम् ..
विरजातीरनीराक्तैः कंपितं मंदवायुभिः .. 112 ..

sanskrit_iast:
kastūrīyuktapatrābjaiḥ puṣpaughaiḥ surabhīkṛtam ..
navapallavasaṃsaktaparapuṣṭarutairyutam..113..
meaning:
कस्तूरीयुक्तपत्राब्जैः पुष्पौघैः सुरभीकृतम् ..
नवपल्लवसंसक्तपरपुष्टरुतैर्युतम्..113..

sanskrit_iast:
kutra helikadaṃbānāṃ kadaṃbaiḥ kamanīyakam ..
maṃdārāṇāṃ caṃpakānāṃ candanānāṃ tathaiva ca ..114..
meaning:
कुत्र हेलिकदंबानां कदंबैः कमनीयकम् ..
मंदाराणां चंपकानां चन्दनानां तथैव च ..114..

sanskrit_iast:
sugaṃdhikusumānāṃ ca gaṃdhena surabhīkṛtam ..
āmrāṇāṃ nāgaraṃgāṇāṃ panasānāṃ tathaiva ca .. 115 ..
meaning:
सुगंधिकुसुमानां च गंधेन सुरभीकृतम् ..
आम्राणां नागरंगाणां पनसानां तथैव च .. 115 ..

sanskrit_iast:
tālānāṃ nārikelānāṃ vṛṃdairvṛṃdārakaṃ vanam ..
jaṃbūnāṃ badarīṇāṃ ca kharjūrāṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ .. 116 ..
meaning:
तालानां नारिकेलानां वृंदैर्वृंदारकं वनम् ..
जंबूनां बदरीणां च खर्जूराणां विशेषतः .. 116 ..

sanskrit_iast:
gurvākāmrātakānāṃ ca jaṃbīrāṇāṃ ca nārada ..
kadalīnāṃ śrīphalānāṃ dāḍimānāṃ manoharaiḥ .. 117 ..
meaning:
गुर्वाकाम्रातकानां च जंबीराणां च नारद ..
कदलीनां श्रीफलानां दाडिमानां मनोहरैः .. 117 ..

sanskrit_iast:
supakvaphalasaṃyuktaiḥ samūhaiśca virājitam ..
pippalīnāṃ ca śālānāmaśvatthānāṃ tathaiva ca .. 118 ..
meaning:
सुपक्वफलसंयुक्तैः समूहैश्च विराजितम् ..
पिप्पलीनां च शालानामश्वत्थानां तथैव च .. 118 ..

sanskrit_iast:
niṃbānāṃ śālmalīnāṃ ca tittiḍīnāṃ ca śobhanaiḥ ..
anyeṣāṃ tarubhedānāṃ saṃkulaiḥ saṃkulaṃ sadā .. 119 ..
meaning:
निंबानां शाल्मलीनां च तित्तिडीनां च शोभनैः ..
अन्येषां तरुभेदानां संकुलैः संकुलं सदा .. 119 ..

sanskrit_iast:
paritaḥ kalpavṛkṣāṇāṃ vṛndairvṛndairvirājitam ..
mallikāmālatīkuṃdaketakīmādhavī latāḥ .. 120 ..
meaning:
परितः कल्पवृक्षाणां वृन्दैर्वृन्दैर्विराजितम् ..
मल्लिकामालतीकुंदकेतकीमाधवी लताः .. 120 ..

sanskrit_iast:
etāsāṃ ca samūhaiśca yūthikābhiḥ samanvitam ..
cārukuṃjakuṭīraistaiḥ paṃcāśatkoṭibhirmune .. 121 ..
meaning:
एतासां च समूहैश्च यूथिकाभिः समन्वितम् ..
चारुकुंजकुटीरैस्तैः पंचाशत्कोटिभिर्मुने .. 121 ..

sanskrit_iast:
ratnapradīpadīpaiśca dhūpena surabhīkṛtaiḥ ..
śṛṃgāradravyayuktaiśca vāsitairgaṃdhavāyubhiḥ .. 122 ..
meaning:
रत्नप्रदीपदीपैश्च धूपेन सुरभीकृतैः ..
शृंगारद्रव्ययुक्तैश्च वासितैर्गंधवायुभिः .. 122 ..

sanskrit_iast:
caṃdanāktaiḥ puṣpatalpairmālājālasamanvitaiḥ ..
madhulubdhamadhughrāṇāṃ kalaśabdaiśca śabditam .. 123 ..
meaning:
चंदनाक्तैः पुष्पतल्पैर्मालाजालसमन्वितैः ..
मधुलुब्धमधुघ्राणां कलशब्दैश्च शब्दितम् .. 123 ..

sanskrit_iast:
ratnālaṃkāraśobhāḍhayairgopīvṛṃdaiśca veṣṭitam ..
paṃcāśatkoṭigopībhī rakṣitaṃ rādhikājñayā ..124..
meaning:
रत्नालंकारशोभाढयैर्गोपीवृंदैश्च वेष्टितम् ..
पंचाशत्कोटिगोपीभी रक्षितं राधिकाज्ञया ..124..
text_mt: filled with the cries of cuckoos perched upon fresh young sprouts. / Here, made lovely by thickets of yellow kadambas, / mandāras, campakas, and sandal trees as well, / and made fragrant by the scent of sweet-smelling blossoms; / a forest adorned with groves of mangoes, oranges, and jackfruits, / as well as palmyras and coconuts; / especially with clusters of rose apples, jujubes, and dates, / betel nuts, hog plums, and limes, O Nārada, / and enchanting plantains, bilvas, and pomegranates, / filled with clusters bearing fully ripened fruits; / constantly crowded with splendid long peppers, / śāla trees, sacred figs, / nimba trees, silk-cotton trees, tamarind trees, / and various other kinds of trees; / adorned on all sides with cluster upon cluster of wish-granting trees, / with climbing plants—mallikā, mālatī, kunda, ketakī, and mādhavī— / joined with swarms of these and with yūthikā jasmines; / with fifty crores of those lovely bower-cottages, O sage, / glowing with gem-lamps, made fragrant with incense, / furnished with articles of lovemaking, and perfumed by fragrant breezes, / with sandalwood-smeared flower beds provided with strings of garlands, / resounding with the sweet humming of bees greedy for honey, / surrounded by multitudes of cowherd maidens adorned with jewel ornaments, / and guarded by fifty crores of cowherd maidens by command of Rādhikā.

sanskrit_iast:
dvātriṃśatkānanaṃ tatra ramyaṃ ramyaṃ manoharam ..
vṛṃdāvanābhyaṃtaritaṃ nirjanasthānamuttamam .. 129 ..

द्वात्रिंशत्काननं तत्र रम्यं रम्यं मनोहरम् ..
वृंदावनाभ्यंतरितं निर्जनस्थानमुत्तमम् .. 129 ..
text_mt: There were thirty-two delightful, exceedingly charming forests, / situated inside Vṛndāvana, an excellent secluded place,

sanskrit_iast:
supakvamadhurasvāduphalairvṛṃdārakaṃ mune ..
goṣṭhānāṃ ca gavāṃ caiva samūhaiśca samanvitam ..126..
meaning:
सुपक्वमधुरस्वादुफलैर्वृंदारकं मुने ..
गोष्ठानां च गवां चैव समूहैश्च समन्वितम् ..126..
text_mt: adorned with fully ripe, sweet, delicious fruits, O sage, / and filled with herds of cows and cowpens,

sanskrit_iast:
puṣpodyānasahasreṇa puṣpitena sugaṃdhinā ..
madhulubdhamadhughrāṇāṃ |samūhena samanvitam ..127..
meaning:
पुष्पोद्यानसहस्रेण पुष्पितेन सुगंधिना ..
मधुलुब्धमधुघ्राणां |समूहेन समन्वितम् ..127..
text_mt: provided with thousands of flowering, fragrant flower gardens, / accompanied by swarms of bees greedy for honey,

sanskrit_iast:
paṃcāśatkoṭigopīnāṃ vilāsaiśca virājitam ..
śrīkṛṣṇatulyarūpāṇāṃ sadratnaguṃṭhitairvaraiḥ ..128..
meaning:
पंचाशत्कोटिगोपीनां विलासैश्च विराजितम् ..
श्रीकृष्णतुल्यरूपाणां सद्रत्नगुंठितैर्वरैः ..128..
text_mt: radiant with the sports of fifty crores of cowherd maidens, / and with noble [youths] of forms equal to Śrī Kṛṣṇa, enveloped in excellent jewels.

sanskrit_iast:
dṛṣṭvā vṛṃdāvanaṃ ramyaṃ yayurgolokamīśvarāḥ ..
parito vartulākāraṃ koṭiyojanavistṛtam .. 129 ...
meaning:
दृष्ट्वा वृंदावनं रम्यं ययुर्गोलोकमीश्वराः ..
परितो वर्तुलाकारं कोटियोजनविस्तृतम् .. 129 ...
text_mt: Having seen charming Vṛndāvana, the lords went to Goloka, / which was circular all around, extending for a crore of yojanas, / enclosed by a jeweled rampart, endowed with four gates, O sage, / and guarded by gatekeepers along with hosts of cowherds;

sanskrit_iast:
ratnaprākārasaṃyuktaṃ caturddhārānvitaṃ mune..
gopānāṃ ca samūhaiśca dvārapālaiḥ samanvitam .. 130 ..
meaning:
रत्नप्राकारसंयुक्तं चतुर्द्धारान्वितं मुने..
गोपानां च समूहैश्च द्वारपालैः समन्वितम् .. 130 ..

sanskrit_iast:
āśramai ratnakhacitairnānābhogasamanvitaiḥ ..
gopīnāṃ kṛṣṇabhṛtyānāṃ paṃcāśatkoṭibhiryutam ..131..
meaning:
आश्रमै रत्नखचितैर्नानाभोगसमन्वितैः ..
गोपीनां कृष्णभृत्यानां पंचाशत्कोटिभिर्युतम् ..131..
text_mt: furnished with fifty crores of jewel-inlaid hermitages / filled with various enjoyments for the cowherd maidens and Kṛṣṇa's servants;

sanskrit_iast:
bhaktānāṃ gopavṛndānāmāśramaiḥ śatakoṭibhiḥ ..
tato'dhikasuvistīrṇaiḥ sadratnagrathitairyutam ..132..
meaning:
भक्तानां गोपवृन्दानामाश्रमैः शतकोटिभिः ..
ततोऽधिकसुविस्तीर्णैः सद्रत्नग्रथितैर्युतम् ..132..
text_mt: with a hundred crores of hermitages for the devoted cowherds, / even more extensive than those, fashioned of fine gems;

sanskrit_iast:
āśramaiḥ pārṣadānāṃ ca tato'dhikavilakṣaṇaiḥ ..
amūlyaratnaracitaiḥ saṃyuktaṃ daśakoṭibhiḥ .. 133 .
meaning:
आश्रमैः पार्षदानां च ततोऽधिकविलक्षणैः ..
अमूल्यरत्नरचितैः संयुक्तं दशकोटिभिः .. 133 .
text_mt: furnished with ten crores of hermitages for the attendants, / even more extraordinary than the former, made of priceless jewels;

sanskrit_iast:
pārṣadapravarāṇāṃ ca śrīkṛṣṇarūpadhāriṇām ..
āśramaiḥ koṭibhiryuktaṃ sadratnena vinirmitaiḥ .. 134..
meaning:
पार्षदप्रवराणां च श्रीकृष्णरूपधारिणाम् ..
आश्रमैः कोटिभिर्युक्तं सद्रत्नेन विनिर्मितैः .. 134..
text_mt: with crores of hermitages built of fine jewels / for the foremost attendants who bear the form of Śrī Kṛṣṇa;

sanskrit_iast:
rādhikāśuddhabhaktānāṃ gopīnāmāśramairvaraiḥ ..
sadratnaracitairdravyairdvātriṃśatkoṭibhiryutam..135..
meaning:
राधिकाशुद्धभक्तानां गोपीनामाश्रमैर्वरैः ..
सद्रत्नरचितैर्द्रव्यैर्द्वात्रिंशत्कोटिभिर्युतम्..135..
text_mt: with thirty-two crores of excellent hermitages built of fine jewels / and goods for the cowherd maidens who are pure devotees of Rādhikā; / and adorned with ten crores of exceedingly lovely mansions / made of gems, jewels, and the like for their handmaidens. / Devotees who have been purified by austerities for a hundred births in the land of Bhārata, / who are devoted to the worship of Hari, and who bring about the dissolution of their karma,

sanskrit_iast:
tāsāṃ ca kikarīṇāṃ ca bhavanaiḥ sumanoharaiḥ..
maṇiratnādiracitaiḥ śobhitaṃ daśakoṭibhiḥ..136..
meaning:
तासां च किकरीणां च भवनैः सुमनोहरैः..
मणिरत्नादिरचितैः शोभितं दशकोटिभिः..136..

sanskrit_iast:
śatajanmatapaḥpūtā bhaktā ye bhārate bhuvi ..
haribhaktiparā ye ca karmanirvāṇakārakāḥ .. 137 ..
meaning:
शतजन्मतपःपूता भक्ता ये भारते भुवि ..
हरिभक्तिपरा ये च कर्मनिर्वाणकारकाः .. 137 ..

sanskrit_iast:
svapne jñāne harerdhyāne viviṣṭamānasā mune ..
rādhākṛṣṇeti kṛṣṇeti prajapaṃto divāniśam .. 138 ..
meaning:
स्वप्ने ज्ञाने हरेर्ध्याने विविष्टमानसा मुने ..
राधाकृष्णेति कृष्णेति प्रजपंतो दिवानिशम् .. 138 ..
text_mt: whose minds are entered into the meditation of Hari in dream and waking knowledge, O sage, / repeating day and night, 'Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa,' 'Kṛṣṇa,'

sanskrit_iast:
paṃcayojanavistīrṇamūrdhvaṃ taddviguṇaṃ mune ..

sanskrit_iast:
pītavastraparīdhānānkrīḍāsaktamanoharān ..
candanokṣitasarvāṃgānratnabhūṣaṇabhūṣitān .. 145 ..

पीतवस्त्रपरीधानान्क्रीडासक्तमनोहरान् ..

text_mt:
Dressed in yellow garments, captivating in their absorption in play, / all their limbs smeared with sandalwood, adorned with jewelled ornaments, // 145
the lords of the gods beheld there the foremost attendants of Hari. / Not far from there, they saw a charming royal highway, // 146
fashioned all around, O sage, with gems that had the appearance of vermilion, / along with sapphire, ruby, diamond, and rucaka stones, // 147
endowed with raised platforms built all about, and a jewelled pavilion, / besmeared with the liquid of sandalwood, aloe, musk, and saffron, // 148
provided with curds, parched grain, fruits, flowers, and sprouts of dūrvā grass, / furnished with sandalwood sprouts tied with fine threads, // 149
adorned with clusters of plantain pillars anointed with saffron, / with pots resting on rings of excellent gems, accompanied by branches and fruit, // 150
anointed with vermilion and saffron, smeared with fragrant sandalwood, / decorated with flower garlands, and adorned with trees, // 151
and surrounded by groups of cowherd women immersed in play. / Having seen these delightful houses, built with jewelled stairs / out of priceless jewels, // 152
charming with garments cleansed by fire, white cāmaras and mirrors, / wonderful with jewelled couches, and adorned with flower garlands, // 153
endowed with sixteen gateways, guarded by gatekeepers, / surrounded all around with moats, enclosed by walls of gems, // 154
and besmeared with the liquid of sandalwood, aloe, musk, and saffron, / those gods, eager to go on, // 155
quickly walked some distance. Then they saw the beautiful / hermitage of Rādhikā, the mistress of the rāsa dance, O Nārada, // 156
built beautifully for the supreme goddess of goddesses, the foremost of the cowherd women, / who is dearer to Kṛṣṇa than his own life, captivating with delightful objects, // 157
entirely beyond description, not to be defined even by the learned, / circular in a very pleasing shape, six gavyūtis in extent, // 158
endowed with a hundred mansions, blazing with the splendour of gems, / excellent, constructed with masses of the essence of priceless jewels, // 159

sanskrit_iast:
dadṛśustatra deveśāḥ pārṣadapravarānhareḥ ..
tato'vidūre dadṛśū rājamārgaṃ manoharam .. 146 ..
meaning:
ददृशुस्तत्र देवेशाः पार्षदप्रवरान्हरेः ..
ततोऽविदूरे ददृशू राजमार्गं मनोहरम् .. 146 ..

sanskrit_iast:
siṃdūrākāramaṇibhiḥ parito racitaṃ mune ..
iṃdranīlaiḥ padmarāgairhīrakai rucakaistathā .. 147 ..
meaning:
सिंदूराकारमणिभिः परितो रचितं मुने ..
इंद्रनीलैः पद्मरागैर्हीरकै रुचकैस्तथा .. 147 ..

sanskrit_iast:
nirmitairvedibhiryuktaṃ parito ratnamaṃḍapam ..
caṃdanāgurukastūrīkuṃkumadravacarcitam .. 148 ..
meaning:
निर्मितैर्वेदिभिर्युक्तं परितो रत्नमंडपम् ..
चंदनागुरुकस्तूरीकुंकुमद्रवचर्चितम् .. 148 ..

sanskrit_iast:
dadhipūrṇalājaphalapuṣpadūrvāṃkurānvitam ..
sūkṣmasūtragraṃthiyuktaśrīkhaṃḍapallavānvitam .. 149 ..
meaning:
दधिपूर्णलाजफलपुष्पदूर्वांकुरान्वितम् ..
सूक्ष्मसूत्रग्रंथियुक्तश्रीखंडपल्लवान्वितम् .. 149 ..

sanskrit_iast:
raṃbhāstaṃbhasamūhaiśca kuṅkumāktairvirājitam ..
sadratnamaṃḍalaghaṭaiḥ phalaśākhāsamanvitaiḥ .. 150 ..
meaning:
रंभास्तंभसमूहैश्च कुङ्कुमाक्तैर्विराजितम् ..
सद्रत्नमंडलघटैः फलशाखासमन्वितैः .. 150 ..

sanskrit_iast:
siṃdūrakuṃkumāktaiśca gaṃdhacaṃdanacarcitaiḥ ..
bhūṣitaiḥ puṣpamālābhiḥ pādapaiḥ paribhūṣitam .. 151 ..
meaning:
सिंदूरकुंकुमाक्तैश्च गंधचंदनचर्चितैः ..
भूषितैः पुष्पमालाभिः पादपैः परिभूषितम् .. 151 ..

sanskrit_iast:
gopikānāṃ samūhaiśca krīḍāsaktaiśca veṣṭitama ..
bahumūlyena ratnena ratnasopānanirmitān .. 152 ..
meaning:
गोपिकानां समूहैश्च क्रीडासक्तैश्च वेष्टितम ..
बहुमूल्येन रत्नेन रत्नसोपाननिर्मितान् .. 152 ..

sanskrit_iast:
vahniśaucāṃśukai ramyaiḥ śvetacāmaradarpaṇaiḥ ..
ratnatalpavicitraiśca puṣpamālyairvirājitāna .. 153 ..
meaning:
वह्निशौचांशुकै रम्यैः श्वेतचामरदर्पणैः ..
रत्नतल्पविचित्रैश्च पुष्पमाल्यैर्विराजितान .. 153 ..

sanskrit_iast:
ṣoḍaśadvārasaṃyuktāndvārapālaiśca rakṣitān ..
paritaḥ parikhāyuktānratnaprākāraveṣṭitān .. 154 ..
meaning:
षोडशद्वारसंयुक्तान्द्वारपालैश्च रक्षितान् ..
परितः परिखायुक्तान्रत्नप्राकारवेष्टितान् .. 154 ..

sanskrit_iast:
caṃdanāgurukastūrīkuṃkumadravacarcitān..
gṛhānmanoramāndṛṣṭvā te devā gamanotsukāḥ .. 155 ..
meaning:
चंदनागुरुकस्तूरीकुंकुमद्रवचर्चितान्..
गृहान्मनोरमान्दृष्ट्वा ते देवा गमनोत्सुकाः .. 155 ..

sanskrit_iast:
jagmuḥ śīghraṃ kiyaddūraṃ dadṛśuḥ sundaraṃ tataḥ ..
āśramaṃ rādhikāyāśca rāseśvaryāśca nārada .. 156 ..
meaning:
जग्मुः शीघ्रं कियद्दूरं ददृशुः सुन्दरं ततः ..
आश्रमं राधिकायाश्च रासेश्वर्याश्च नारद .. 156 ..

sanskrit_iast:
devādhidevyā gopīnāṃ varāyāścārunirmitam ..
prāṇādhikāyāḥ kṛṣṇasya ramyadravyamanoharam .. 157 ..

sanskrit_iast:

सुचारुवर्तुलाकारं षड्गव्यूतिप्रमाणकम् .. 158 ..

sanskrit_iast:
śatamaṃdirasaṃyuktaṃ jvalitaṃ ratnatejasā ..
amūlyaratnasārāṇāṃ cayaurviracitaṃ varam .. 159 ..

अमूल्यरत्नसाराणां चयौर्विरचितं वरम् .. 159 ..

sanskrit_iast:
durlaṃghyābhirgabhīrābhiḥ parikhābhiḥ suśobhitam ..
kalpavṛkṣaiḥ parivṛtaṃ puṣpodyānaśatāṃtaram .. 160 ..
meaning:
दुर्लंघ्याभिर्गभीराभिः परिखाभिः सुशोभितम् ..
कल्पवृक्षैः परिवृतं पुष्पोद्यानशतांतरम् .. 160 ..
text_mt:
beautifully adorned with deep moats difficult to cross, / surrounded by wish-granting trees, with intervals of hundreds of flower gardens, // 160
enclosed by walls studded with precious gems, / having excellent jewelled platforms, and provided with seven gates, // 161
joined with colourful jewelled paintings, wondrous and circular, O sage. / Starting from the seven principal gates in succession, in succession, O sage, // 162
it was endowed with sixteen gates on every side as well. / Having seen the rampart, a thousand bows in height, // 163
resplendent with its brilliance, beautiful with clusters of small pots made of excellent jewels, / the gods were filled with the greatest astonishment. // 164
Then, circumambulating it, they walked a short distance in joy. / As they advanced, that hermitage fell behind them. // 165
They saw other hermitages of the cowherds and cowherd women, / fashioned of priceless jewels, a hundred crores in number, O sage. // 166
Looking continually around at every hermitage of the cowherds, / and other charming, fresh, and delightful ones of the cowherd women, // 167
and seeing the entire Goloka, the gods had their limbs thrilled with horripilation. / That same round, charming forest was Vṛndāvana; // 368
they saw the Śataśṛṅga mountain, and outside it the Virajā river. / The gods went to that Virajā, and saw only empty space. // 169
And Goloka rested on the air, wonderful, made of excellent gems, / fashioned by the will of the Lord by virtue of Rādhikā's command, // 170
endowed with thousands of lakes, an abode of pure auspiciousness. / The gods also saw a most charming dance there, // 171
and delightful singing with beautiful melodies, celebrating the virtues of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. / Merely upon hearing the nectar of that song, the gods swooned, O sage. // 172
Regaining consciousness in a moment, their minds fixed on Kṛṣṇa, / those gods beheld the greatest wonder, charming in every place. // 173
They saw all the cowherd women assuming diverse disguises:

sanskrit_iast:
sumūlyaratnakhacitaprākāraiḥ pariveṣṭitam ..
sadratnavedikāyuktairyuktaṃ dvāraiśca saptabhiḥ .. 161 ..
meaning:
सुमूल्यरत्नखचितप्राकारैः परिवेष्टितम् ..
सद्रत्नवेदिकायुक्तैर्युक्तं द्वारैश्च सप्तभिः .. 161 ..

sanskrit_iast:

pradhānasaptadvārebhyaḥ kramaśaḥ kramaśo mune .. 162 ..

संयुक्तरत्नचित्रैश्च विचित्रैर्वर्तुलं मुने ..
प्रधानसप्तद्वारेभ्यः क्रमशः क्रमशो मुने .. 162 ..

sanskrit_iast:
sarvato'pi tatastatra ṣoḍaśadvārasaṃyutam ..
devā ddaṣṭvā ca prākāraṃ sahasradhanurucchritam .. 163 ..
meaning:
सर्वतोऽपि ततस्तत्र षोडशद्वारसंयुतम् ..
देवा द्दष्ट्वा च प्राकारं सहस्रधनुरुच्छ्रितम् .. 163 ..

sanskrit_iast:
sadratnakṣudrakalaśasamūhaiḥ sumanoharaiḥ ..
pradīptaṃ tejasā ramyaṃ paramaṃ vismayaṃ yayuḥ .. 164 ..
meaning:
सद्रत्नक्षुद्रकलशसमूहैः सुमनोहरैः ..
प्रदीप्तं तेजसा रम्यं परमं विस्मयं ययुः .. 164 ..

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya kiyaddūraṃ yayurmudā ..
purato gacchatāṃ teṣāṃ paścādbhūtastadāśramaḥ .. 165 ..
meaning:
ततः प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य कियद्दूरं ययुर्मुदा ..
पुरतो गच्छतां तेषां पश्चाद्भूतस्तदाश्रमः .. 165 ..

sanskrit_iast:
gopānāṃ gopikānāṃ ca dadṛśuścāśramānparān ..
amūlyaratnaracitāñchatakoṭimitānmune .. 166 ..
meaning:
गोपानां गोपिकानां च ददृशुश्चाश्रमान्परान् ..
अमूल्यरत्नरचिताञ्छतकोटिमितान्मुने .. 166 ..

sanskrit_iast:
darśaṃdarśaṃ ca parito gopānāṃ sarvamāśramam ..
gopikānāṃ cāparaṃ vā ramyaṃ ramyaṃ navaṃnavam .. 167 ..
meaning:
दर्शंदर्शं च परितो गोपानां सर्वमाश्रमम् ..
गोपिकानां चापरं वा रम्यं रम्यं नवंनवम् .. 167 ..

sanskrit_iast:
golokaṃ nikhilaṃ dṛṣṭvā pulakāṃgaṃ yayuḥ surāḥ ..
tadeva vartulākāraṃ ramyaṃ vṛṃdāvanaṃ vanam .. 368 ..
meaning:
गोलोकं निखिलं दृष्ट्वा पुलकांगं ययुः सुराः ..
तदेव वर्तुलाकारं रम्यं वृंदावनं वनम् .. 368 ..

sanskrit_iast:
dadṛśuḥ śataśṛṃgaṃ ca tadbahirvirajānadīm ..

sanskrit_iast:
vāyvādhāraṃ ca golokaṃ sadratnamayamadbhutam ..
īśvarecchāvinirmāṇaṃ rādhikājñānubaṃdhanāt .. 170 ..

वाय्वाधारं च गोलोकं सद्रत्नमयमद्भुतम् ..
ईश्वरेच्छाविनिर्माणं राधिकाज्ञानुबंधनात् .. 170 ..

sanskrit_iast:
yuktaṃ sahasraiḥ sarasāṃ kevalaṃ maṃgalālayam ..
nṛtyaṃ ca dadṛśustatra devāśca sumanoharam .. 171 ..
meaning:
युक्तं सहस्रैः सरसां केवलं मंगलालयम् ..
नृत्यं च ददृशुस्तत्र देवाश्च सुमनोहरम् .. 171 ..

sanskrit_iast:
sutānaṃ cārusaṃgītaṃ rādhākṛṣṇaguṇānvitam ..
śrutvaiva gītapīyūṣaṃ mūrchāmāpuḥ surā mune .. 172 ..
meaning:
सुतानं चारुसंगीतं राधाकृष्णगुणान्वितम् ..
श्रुत्वैव गीतपीयूषं मूर्छामापुः सुरा मुने .. 172 ..

sanskrit_iast:
kṣaṇena cetanāṃ prāpya te devāḥ kṛṣṇamānasāḥ ..
dadṛśuḥ paramāścaryaṃ sthānesthāne manoharam .. 173 ..
meaning:
क्षणेन चेतनां प्राप्य ते देवाः कृष्णमानसाः ..
ददृशुः परमाश्चर्यं स्थानेस्थाने मनोहरम् .. 173 ..

sanskrit_iast:
dadṛśurgopikāḥ sarvā nānāveṣavidhāyikāḥ ..
kāścinmṛdaṃgahastāśca kāścidvīṇākarā varāḥ .. 174 ..
meaning:
ददृशुर्गोपिकाः सर्वा नानावेषविधायिकाः ..
काश्चिन्मृदंगहस्ताश्च काश्चिद्वीणाकरा वराः .. 174 ..

sanskrit_iast:
kāściccāmarahastāśca karatālakarāḥ parāḥ ..
kāścidyaṃtravādyahastā ratnanūpuraśobhitāḥ .. 175 ..
meaning:
काश्चिच्चामरहस्ताश्च करतालकराः पराः ..
काश्चिद्यंत्रवाद्यहस्ता रत्ननूपुरशोभिताः .. 175 ..

sanskrit_iast:
sadratnakiṃkiṇījālaśabdena śabditā varāḥ ..
kāścinmastakakuṃbhāśca nṛtyabhedamanorathāḥ .. 176 ..
meaning:
सद्रत्नकिंकिणीजालशब्देन शब्दिता वराः ..
काश्चिन्मस्तककुंभाश्च नृत्यभेदमनोरथाः .. 176 ..

sanskrit_iast:
puṃveṣanāyikāḥ kāścitkāścittāsāṃ ca nāyikāḥ ..
kṛṣṇaveṣadharāḥ kāścidrādhāveṣadharāḥ parāḥ .. 177 ..
meaning:
पुंवेषनायिकाः काश्चित्काश्चित्तासां च नायिकाः ..
कृष्णवेषधराः काश्चिद्राधावेषधराः पराः .. 177 ..

sanskrit_iast:
kāścitsaṃyogaviratāḥ kāścidāliṃgane ratāḥ ..
krīḍāsaktāśca tā dṛṣṭvā sasmitā jagadīśvarāḥ .. 178 ..

There are thirty-three companions of Rādhikā, cowherd women / whose adornment is beyond description; hear their names: // 181

Beyond and above the cosmic egg there is no realm; / above it, everything consists of the void, and there creation ends.
Below the seven netherworlds, there is no creation; / below them is water, darkness, impassable and invisible. / Hear from me everything up to the cosmic egg and beyond it.
Thus ends the fourth chapter, entitled “Description of Goloka,” in the dialogue between Nārāyaṇa and Nārada, in the Śrīkṛṣṇajanmakhaṇḍa of the glorious Mahāpurāṇa Brahmavaivarta.

text_mt:
Glorious Nārāyaṇa said: / Having seen all of Goloka, those gods, glad at heart, / came once more to the principal gateway of Rādhā.
It was built of fine gems and jewels, furnished with a pair of platforms / of gems having the appearance of turmeric mingled with diamonds,
and adorned with door-leaves crafted of priceless jewels. / At the gate they saw appointed the peerless Vīrabhānu,
seated upon a jewelled throne, adorned with jewelled ornaments, / clad in yellow garments, and radiant with a crown of fine gems.
To the doorkeeper at that gate, wonderful and most marvellous with varied wonders, / the gods gladly made their entire petition.
The gatekeeper spoke without hesitation to the lords of the gods: / “I am not able to permit entry at this time without an order.”
He dispatched attendants to the abode of Śrī Kṛṣṇa; / having obtained Hari’s permission, O sage, he granted the gods passage.
Having conversed with him, the gods went to the excellent second gate, / which was even more wondrous than that one, beautiful and very enchanting.
At that gate they saw appointed Candrabhānu, O Nārada, / a youth, dark-complexioned, handsome, an excellent holder of a golden staff,
seated upon a jewelled throne, adorned with jewelled ornaments, / and attended by a host of five hundred thousand cowherds.
Having conversed with him, the gods went to the excellent third gate, / which was exceedingly beautiful, wondrous, and blazing with the splendour of gems.
At that gate they saw appointed Sūryabhānu, O Nārada, / two-armed, with a flute in his hand, a youth dark and beautiful,
with his cheeks adorned by a pair of jewelled earrings, / holding a jewelled staff, supreme, a paramount attendant of Rādhā and the Lord,
surrounded by nine hundred thousand cowherds like a king of kings. / Having conversed with him, the gods went on to the fourth gate,
distinct from the others, charming, and brightly blazing with the splendour of gems,

सस्मितं सुन्दरवरं श्रीखण्डतिलकोज्ज्वलम् .. 29 ..
text_mt:
Smiling, most handsome, radiant with a sandal-paste tilaka,
with lower lip like a bandhujīva flower, adorned with gem-encrusted earrings,
rich in the splendor of all ornaments, holding an exquisite staff of gems,
and accompanied by twelve hundred thousand young cowherd boys.
Then the gods quickly went to the desired ninth gate,
built of diamonds and fine jewels, provided with four platforms,
and adorned with networks of garlands fashioned into unprecedented designs.
There they saw the gatekeeper Subala of graceful form,
rich in the beauty of varied ornaments, worthy of ornaments, charming,
accompanied by twelve hundred thousand diamond[-like cowherds], exceedingly delightful.
Having spoken to him as he held a staff in hand, the gods proceeded to another gate.
Seeing the splendid tenth gate, they were struck with wonder;
it was entirely indescribable, unseen and unheard of before, O sage!
They saw the handsome gatekeeper Sudāman,
of indescribable beauty, charming, equal to Kṛṣṇa,
surrounded by multitudes of two million cowherds.
Having seen him with his staff in hand, the gods went on to another gate:
the gate named the eleventh, beautifully varied, great and wonderful.
Stationed there as gatekeeper was Śrīdāman, the lord of Vraja,
like a son to Rādhikā, dressed in yellow garments,
seated upon a gem-studded throne wrought of priceless jewels,
adorned with priceless gemmed ornaments, exceedingly handsome,
resplendent with sandal, agallochum, musk, and saffron,
radiant with fine gem-encrusted earrings befitting his cheeks and temples,
shining with a wondrous crown wrought of the finest precious gems,
his entire body adorned with garlands of blooming jasmine flowers,
surrounded by ten million cowherds, more brilliant than the greatest of kings.
Having spoken to him, the gods gladly went to the gate named the twelfth,
provided with platforms built of priceless gems,
rare to all, wondrous, unseen, and unheard of, O sage,

sanskrit_iast:

प्रफुल्लमालतीमालाजालैर्वक्षस्थलोज्ज्वलैः .. 58 ..
text_mt:
situated upon walls of diamond, variegated, lovely, and most enchanting.
Stationed at the gate, the gods saw excellent cowherd women,
endowed with fresh youth, adorned with jewel ornaments,
wearing yellow garments, adorned with heavy masses of braided hair,
their whole limbs adorned with networks of fragrant jasmine garlands,
adorned with jeweled bracelets, armlets, and jeweled anklets,
their cheeks resplendent with pairs of jeweled earrings,
anointed with liquid paste of sandal, agallochum, musk, and saffron,
bending under the weight of their plump hips, laden with the burden of their buttocks,
the foremost among hundreds of millions of gopīs, and dearest even to Hari.
Seeing those millions of gopīs, the gods were filled with wonder.
Having spoken to them, they joyfully went to another gate, O sage.
Then gradually, O brāhmaṇa, at the three gates there,
they saw the foremost of cowherd women, most charming,
the best of the best, lovely, fortunate, revered, and beautiful,
all endowed with good fortune, dear to Rādhikā,
adorned with lovely ornaments, bursting with fresh youth.
Thus having seen the three gates—unheard of, wonderful, beyond the knowledge of dreams,
unseen, exceedingly lovely, and undefinable even by the wise—
and having spoken with those women, the astonished gods, those lords,
went to the charming sixteenth gate leading to the interior of Rādhikā's abode,
the foremost of all, guarded by hosts of cowherd women,
surrounded by multitudes of her thirty-three companions, O sage.
Those women were indescribable, endowed with diverse virtues,
full of beauty and youth, adorned with jeweled ornaments,
adorned with jeweled bracelets, armlets, and gemmed anklets,
their waists adorned with strings of fine jeweled tinkling bells,
their cheeks resplendent with pairs of jeweled earrings,
their chests radiant with networks of blooming jasmine garlands,

sanskrit_iast:
śaratpārvaṇapadmānāṃ prabhāṃ muṣṇanmukheṃdubhiḥ ..
pārijātaprasūnānāṃ mālājālena veṣṭitaiḥ .. .. 59 ..
meaning:
शरत्पार्वणपद्मानां प्रभां मुष्णन्मुखेंदुभिः ..
पारिजातप्रसूनानां मालाजालेन वेष्टितैः .. .. 59 ..
text_mt:
stealing the splendor of autumnal full-moon lotuses with their moon-like faces,
encircled by networks of garlands of pārijāta blossoms,
with lower lips like ripe bimba fruit, smiling lotus-like faces,
adorned with rows of teeth resembling ripe pomegranate seeds,
with the beautiful complexion of the campaka flower, slender at the waist, O sage,
resplendent with noses adorned with elephant-pearls,
stealing the beauty of the graceful beaks of the king of birds,
bent under the heavy burden of breasts firm as the temples of lordly elephants,
afflicted by the weight of their plump hips, their minds fixed upon Mukunda's feet.
Without blinking, the gods beheld both the gate and those maidens.
It was beautified by a pair of platforms set with shining, lovely gems,
always fitted with clusters of pillars of emeralds,
with their middles shining with cinnabar-colored gems,
adorned with networks of garlands of pārijāta blossoms,
scented everywhere by the breezes fragrant from contacting them.
Having seen that supreme wonder, the inner realm of Rādhikā, the gods,
whose sole desire was the vision of Śrī Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet,
spoke to them and quickly went forward, their bodies thrilled with horripilation,
filled with tears from surging devotion, their necks slightly bowed.
From nearby the gods saw the excellent inner chamber of Rādhikā,
a charming quadrangle situated in the midst of palaces,
fashioned excellently from the quintessence of priceless gems,
adorned with pillars of diverse jewels and gems joined with diamonds,
resplendent with networks of garlands of pārijāta flowers,
adorned, O sage, with heaps of pearls, rubies, white chowries, mirrors,
and pitchers made from the essence of priceless jewels,
its lovely courtyard adorned with clusters of gem-encrusted pillars
provided with sandal-tree shoots tied with knots of silk thread,
endowed with liquid paste of sandal, agallochum, musk, and saffron,
and with white grain, white flowers, coral, fruits, and rice grains.

sanskrit_iast:
pīnaśroṇibharārtaiśca mukuṃdapadamānasaiḥ ..
nimeṣarahitā devā dvāraṃ ca dadṛśuśca tāḥ ..63..
meaning:
पीनश्रोणिभरार्तैश्च मुकुंदपदमानसैः ..

sanskrit_iast:
lasadramaṇiratnaiśca vedikāyugmaśobhitam ..
harinmaṇīnāṃ staṃbhānāṃ samūhaiḥ saṃyutaṃ sadā .. 64 ..
meaning:
लसद्रमणिरत्नैश्च वेदिकायुग्मशोभितम् ..
हरिन्मणीनां स्तंभानां समूहैः संयुतं सदा .. 64 ..

sanskrit_iast:
siṃdūrākāramaṇibhirmadhyasthalavirājitaiḥ ..
pārijāta prasūnānāṃ mālājālairvibhūṣitam .. 65 ..
meaning:
सिंदूराकारमणिभिर्मध्यस्थलविराजितैः ..
पारिजात प्रसूनानां मालाजालैर्विभूषितम् .. 65 ..
text_mt: adorned with garlands of pārijāta blossoms,

sanskrit_iast:
tatsaṃsparśairgaṃdhavāhaiḥ sarvatra surabhīkṛtam ..
dṛṣṭvā tatparamāścaryaṃ rādhikābhyaṃtaraṃ surāḥ .. 66 ..
meaning:
तत्संस्पर्शैर्गंधवाहैः सर्वत्र सुरभीकृतम् ..
दृष्ट्वा तत्परमाश्चर्यं राधिकाभ्यंतरं सुराः .. 66 ..

sanskrit_iast:
śrīkṛṣṇacaraṇāṃbhojadarśanaikamanorathāḥ ..
tāḥ saṃbhāṣya yayuḥ śīghraṃ pulakāṃcitavigrahāḥ .. 67 ..

text_mt: [adorned with] leaves, dūrvā grass, and unbroken grains, decorated with auspicious waved offerings of parched grains, / with jeweled pitchers bearing fruits and covered with vermilion and saffron; / adorned with garlands of pārijāta blossoms, / and made fragrant everywhere by breezes laden with flowers; / adorned with everything indescribable and unspecified in substance, / with whatever objects are rare in the cosmic egg; / beautifully adorned with clusters of pārijāta blossom garlands, / with charming [gopīs] on jeweled couches, draped in fine garments; / with hundreds of millions of jeweled pitchers, Nārada, and jeweled vessels / that were priceless and beautiful, adorned with those very things; / resounding with the sweet tones of various instruments, / and well-attuned to the singing of the gopīs accompanied by harps and vīṇās; / enchanted by the sounds of instruments and of mṛdaṅga drums, Nārada; / surrounded by multitudes of cowherds equal to Kṛṣṇa; / shining with multitude upon multitude of the gopīs, companions of Rādhā; / filled with the sweet sounds of songs whose verses extolled the virtues of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. / Seeing the interior thus, the gods were amazed; / they heard the sweet singing and saw the supreme dance. / All the gods stood there, their minds absorbed in meditation alone; / the lords of the thirty [gods] beheld a delightful jeweled throne, / a hundred bows in measure and circular in form all around, / furnished with arrays of small vessels made of genuine jewels, / and adorned with wonderful figurines, flowers, and variegated groves. / There [they saw] a mass of splendor with radiance equal to millions of suns, / blazing with light, O Brahman, a great and wondrous marvel; / measuring seven tāla trees, it pervaded upwards in all directions, / eclipsing the radiance of all, free from any weary effort, / all-pervading, the seed of all, obstructing the eyes, supreme. / Having seen that embodiment of radiance, those gods, intent on meditation, / bowed with supreme devotion, their necks bent low in reverence;

text_mt: their eyes filled with tears from the union with supreme bliss, / all their limbs thrilled with horripilation, their desires and longings fulfilled. / Having bowed to that Lord whose form is radiance, the lords of the thirty [gods] / stood up there and, immersed in meditation, remained before that splendor. / Having thus meditated, the creator of the worlds placed his palms together, / setting Śaṅkara on his right and Dharma on his left, O Nārada; / and from an abundance of devotion, his mind fixed in single-pointed meditation, / he praised the Lord, the Paramātman, higher than the highest, beyond the gunas: / Brahmā said: / I bow to that form of radiance, the best, the most worthy, the granter of boons, the cause of the bestowers of boons, / the cause of all beings. / I bow to that form of radiance, the blessing among blessings, auspicious, bestowing auspiciousness, / the support of all auspicious things. / I bow to that form of radiance, present everywhere, untainted, whose form is the Self, higher than the highest, / inactive and inconceivable. / I bow to that form of radiance, with gunas and devoid of gunas, Brahman, whose form is light, eternal, / both with form and formless. / I bow to that form of radiance, indescribable, manifest and unmanifest, single, / consisting of his own will, embodying all forms. / Supreme, assuming three forms to differentiate the three gunas— / all [beings] were made by a part of you; how can they know that which is beyond the Veda? / I bow to that form of radiance, the support of all, the form of all, the seed of all, seedless, / the end of all, and infinite. / That which possesses the six qualities can be perceived and described by the wise; / how can I describe that which is to be perceived? I bow to that form of radiance. / I bow to that form of radiance, bodiless yet possessed of a body, with senses yet beyond the senses, / that which is no witness yet the witness of all. / I bow to that form of radiance, able to go yet footless, without eyes yet seeing all, / without hands or mouth yet the enjoyer. / Good people are able to describe that substance which is set forth in the Veda;

text_mt: I bow to that form of radiance which is not set forth in the Veda. / I bow to that form of radiance which is the Lord of all yet without a lord, the beginning of all yet beginningless, / identical with all yet without a self. / I am the creator of the universe, myself the father of the Vedas; / Dharma is the protector, Hara the destroyer; yet none of us are able to praise you. / By service to you, this Dharma was appointed to protect [it]; / and by your command he is the destroyer, at the time designated by you. / I am the maker of entire creation through service to your lotus feet; / you are the giver of fruits to those who perform action, and our Lord, the master of devotees.

text_mt:
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Standing before the splendour after meditating and praising,
the gods saw a lovely body within the splendour, // 1
having the complexion of a water-laden cloud, smiling, captivating the mind,
an exceedingly delighting form that enchants the minds of the three worlds, // 2
with glittering makara-shaped earrings shining upon both cheeks and temples,
adorned with lotus feet that have anklets of fine gems, // 3
radiant in costly garments with the lustre of fire-purified turmeric,
adorned with delightful ornaments fashioned at will in play // 4
from the finest of precious jewels, ornaments themselves adorned by his very form,
charming with bimba-fruit lips touching a playful flute, // 5
looking on with gracious eyes, eager to show favour to his devotees,
his chest radiant with armour set with fine jewels and pearls, // 6
blazing with the bright splendour of the fine Kaustubha gem attached to it.
And there within that splendour they saw a lovely-limbed woman named Rādhikā, // 7
gazing with sidelong glance at her beloved who was looking at her with a smile,
radiant with a row of teeth that mocked a string of pearls, // 8
her face gracious with a gentle smile, eyes like autumn lotuses,
her face lovely, mocking the brilliance of the autumn full moon, // 9
her charming face possessing lower and upper lips that robbed the glow of the bandhujīva flower,
her lotus feet adorned with a pair of tinkling anklets, // 4.6.10
shining with rows of nails that stole the lustre of precious gems,
her feet adorned below with red dye, having covered the lustre of saffron, // 11
her hips adorned with a girdle of the finest priceless gems,
gleaming and bright with costly garments purified by fire, // 12
with waist adorned with tiny bells made from the finest great jewels,
adorned with necklaces of fine gems, armlets, and bracelets, // 13
with earrings fashioned from the best of precious gems, bright against her cheeks,
adorned above her ears with ear-ornaments of precious gems, // 14
with a pearl from the royal elephant at the tip of her nose resembling the beak of the king of birds,
adorned with a dense mass of braided hair embellished with a garland of mālatī flowers, // 15

text_mt:
her chest gracefully adorned with a garland of the finest Kaustubhas,
her upper garment radiant with an array of garlands of pārijāta blossoms, // 16
her fingers adorned with heaps of jewel-set rings,
adorned with beautiful conch-shell ornaments fashioned into fine threads, // 17
made of heavenly conch shell and adorned with diverse colours,
splendid with strings made from clusters of the finest choice gems, // 18
her lovely body veiled with the lustre of molten gold,
charming with hips and waist, bent slightly under the weight of swelling breasts, // 19
adorned with all manner of ornaments that were themselves adorned by her beauty.
Seeing that supreme sovereign lady, all the gods were amazed;
all those gods, having all their desires fulfilled, praised her. // 4.6.20
Brahmā said:
May the bee of my mind ever wander, O Lord, at the lotus of your feet in loving devotion;
give me firm, fully mature devotion and servitude to you, which is the medicine to quench the burning pain born from the enjoyment of worldly power! // 21
Śaṅkara said:
My fish-like mind, submerged in the ocean of worldly existence, constantly roams in this terrible well of saṃsāra;
take away this utterly blameworthy worldly concern that is the essence of creation and dissolution, and grant me devotion to your lotus feet! // 22
Dharma said:
O my Lord, may my association with your own people be a sharp sword for cutting the bonds of worldly objects;
give me devotion to your lotus feet birth after birth, the sole cause of granting a place at your lotus feet! // 23
Having thus offered praise, their minds single-pointedly fulfilled,
they stood before the fulfiller of desires, the lord of Rādhikā. // 24
Hearing the praise of the gods, the storehouse of compassion,
his lotus face smiling, addressed them with words beneficial and true. // 25
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Stay, come forward, O gods—you are mine, there is no doubt of this;
it is not fitting now to enquire after the welfare of those who have Śiva as their refuge. // 26
Be free from care right here; what anxiety can there be for you when I am present?

text_mt:
"I reside in all living beings; indeed, I become visible through praise.
I know with certainty whatever intention you have.
And whatever good or evil deed will indeed come to pass in its own time.
O gods, every deed, whether great or small, is wrought by Time.
In their own seasons the trees are ever bearing fruit and blossoming;
ripe are their fruits in time, and in time endowed with ripe fruits.
Happiness, suffering, misfortune, prosperity, grief, anxiety, good and evil,
all resting upon the fruits of one's own deeds, arise at their proper time.
Indeed, no one is dear or unpleasing to anyone in the three worlds;
in time, through the force of circumstances, those disliked become dear, and the dear become disliked.
Kings and Manus on earth were seen by you here;
by the ripening of the fruit of their own deeds, all have gone under the sway of Time.
And the moment that has just now passed for you in Goloka,
by that very moment seven manvantaras have passed on earth.
Seven Indras have passed there, and now there is an eighth lord of the gods.
My wheel of Time turns continually day and night;
Indras, Manus, and kings have all gone under the sway of Time.
Renown and merit on earth are now reduced to mere tales.
Even now, many kings, wicked and blasphemers of Hari,
have arisen on earth, possessing great strength and prowess.
All those kings will certainly pass under the sway of death.
Even though this Time has arrived, the wind blows constantly,
fire burns, and the sun blazes indeed by my command.
Diseases dwell in bodies, death moves among living beings,
these clouds rain, and all the gods [act] by my command.
Brahmins intent on brahminhood, ascetics rich in penance intent on austerity,
Brahma-ṛṣis intent on Brahman, and yogins intent on yoga,
all of them, terrified of fear of me, are devoted each to their own deeds and duties.

text_mt:
And my devotees, being free from doubt, eradicate karma.
O gods, I am the Time of Time, the ordainer of the creator itself,
the destroyer of the destroyer, the protector of the protector, higher than the highest.
By my command this one is the destroyer, and therefore is called Hara by name.
You are the creator of the universe for the sake of creation, and [Viṣṇu] is the protector for the guarding of dharma.
From Brahmā down to a blade of grass, I am the sovereign of all.
I am the dispenser of the fruit of one's own deeds, the eradicator of karma.
When I shall destroy them, who could be their protector?
And whom I shall protect, no one at all is their slayer.
I alone am the destroyer, the creator, and the protector of all.
Yet I am not able to destroy my devotees, who possess eternal bodies.
Devotees are ever my followers, intent on worshipping my feet;
I am constantly near the devotees for the sake of their protection.
All things in the cosmic egg perish and are born again and again;
my devotees do not perish, free from doubt and free from danger.
Therefore, all the wise desire servitude [to me], not boons;
those who beg me for servitude are blessed, while others are deceived.
Fear of birth, death, old age, disease, and the torments of Yama
belongs to other actors of deeds, but never to my devotees.
Devotees are not tainted by sins or by merits, as are all [other] agents of actions;
I surely shake off the experiences of their karma.
I am the life-breath of my devotees, and the devotees are my life-breath;
they meditate on me constantly, and I remember them day and night.
The discus named Sudarśana has sixteen spokes and is exceedingly sharp;
even a sixteenth part of its splendour does not exist in any living beings.
Placing that desired discus near my devotee for protection,
I have no peace and no joy [until] I go near them.
I have no peace in Vaikuṇṭha, nor in Goloka beside Rādhikā;

text_mt:
wherever those devotees of mine abide, there I abide day and night.
Rādhā, dearer than life, dwells upon my chest day and night;
you are dearer than life, Lakṣmī is, but none is dearer to me than a devotee.
And whatever item is offered by a devotee with devotion, O lords of gods, I eat;
what is offered by a non-devotee I do not eat; Bali himself surely consumes it.
Abandoning wife, sons, and kin, they meditate on me day and night;
leaving you, I constantly remember them day and night.
When the wicked surely inflict harm upon my devotees,
upon Brahmins, upon cows, upon sacrifices, and upon deities,
they perish without delay, just like blades of grass in fire;
no one is their protector when I have arrived as their slayer.
I will go to earth, O gods; go to your own abodes.
And you too, in the form of your portions, go quickly to the earthly plane."
Having spoken thus, the Lord of the worlds called the cowherd men and cowherd women
and spoke sweet words, truthful and suited to the occasion:
"O cowherds and cowherdesses, listen! Go to the supreme Vraja of Nanda.
Go swiftly to the house of Vṛṣabhānu, you too, O Rādhikā!
The beloved of Vṛṣabhānu, the virtuous Kalāvatī, [sister of] Nandagopa,
is the daughter of Subala, born from a portion of Kamalā,
the mind-born daughter of the ancestors, blessed and honoured among women.
Formerly, through the curse of Durvāsas, her birth took place in a house in Vraja.
Take birth in her house, and go quickly to the Vraja of Nanda;
I will take you in the form of a child, O lotus-faced one!
You are dearer to me than life, O Rādhā, and I am dearer to you than life;
there is nothing distinct between us two, forever indeed of one body."
Hearing this, Rādhikā wept there, overcome with love;
with the cakora-birds of her eyes, O sage, she drank the moon of Hari's face.
[The Lord said:] "Take birth, O cowherds and cowherdesses, on the earthly plane,
in the auspicious homes of the foremost cowherds."

text_mt:
In the meantime, everyone saw an excellent chariot, / adorned with the finest diamonds and precious jewels, / 70
beautified with a hundred thousand white chowries and tens of thousands of mirrors, / adorned with fine, fire-purified ochre garments, / 71
richly decorated with a thousand vessels of excellent gems, / shining with networks of garlands of pārijāta blossoms, / 72
accompanied by choice attendants, auspicious, made of gold, / the very embodiment of splendor, peerless, radiant as a hundred suns. / 73
Seated upon it, [they saw] a dark, handsome, charming man, / holding the conch, discus, mace, and lotus, clad in excellent yellow garments, / 74
wearing a diadem and earrings, adorned with a forest garland, / anointed with paste of sandalwood, agallochum, musk, and saffron, / 75
four-armed, smiling-faced, eager to grant grace to his devotees, / adorned with the finest ornaments made from the essence of prime jewels. / 76
To his left [stood] a charming goddess, fair-complexioned and captivating, / richly endowed with the beauty of gem ornaments, adorned with yellow garments, / 77
with a face like the full autumn moon, eyes like autumn lotuses, / lips like ripe bimba fruit, smiling and delightful, / 78
holding a flute, a vīṇā, and a book in her hands, eager to grant grace to devotees— / the presiding goddess of learning, the embodiment of wisdom, Sarasvatī. / 79
To his right [stood] another charming [goddess], radiant as a hundred moons, / lustrous with the hue of molten gold, smiling, exceedingly delightful, / 80
her beautiful cheeks adorned with earrings of fine gems, / clothed in priceless garments inlaid with priceless jewels, / 81
adorned with armlets and bracelets of priceless gems, / accompanied by the tinkling sound of anklets made from the essence of fine gems, / 82
her waist graced with a girdle of supreme jewels, / her chest bright with garlands of pārijāta blossoms, / 83
her braid of hair adorned with garlands of blooming mālatī flowers, / beautifully adorned with a face outshining the radiance of the autumn moon, / 84

text_mt:
bearing a sindūra mark dotted with a drop of musk, / her autumn-lotus eyes painted with exquisite collyrium, / 85
holding a play-lotus attached to a thousand petals, / looking with side-glances at Nārāyaṇa as he looked at her. / 86
Quickly descending from the chariot along with his wife and his attendants, / he entered the delightful assembly filled with cowherds and gopīs. / 87
The gods, gopīs, and cowherds stood joyfully with folded hands, / as hymns of praise from the Sāmaveda were sung by the divine rṣis. / 88
Going forward, the god Nārāyaṇa merged into the body of Kṛṣṇa; / and beholding that supreme wonder, they were all struck with amazement. / 89
In the meantime, descending from a golden chariot right there, / Viṣṇu himself, the protector and lord of the worlds, / 90
arrived, four-armed, adorned with a forest garland, / clad in yellow garments, glorious, smiling, exceedingly charming, / 91
richly adorned with all kinds of ornaments, radiant as ten million suns. / Seeing him, they arose, bowed down, and praised him, O sage. / 92
And he too merged right there into the body of Rādhikā's lord; / seeing that great wonder, they were filled with the highest amazement. / 93
When the dweller of Śvetadvīpa had merged into Hari's body, / in the meantime there swiftly arrived in great haste / 94
one resembling pure crystal, known by the name Saṃkarṣaṇa, / the thousand-headed Puruṣa, radiant as a hundred suns. / 95
Seeing that embodiment of Viṣṇu arrive, all praised him. / And having approached with bent shoulders, he praised the lord of Rādhikā. / 96
With a thousand heads he bowed down in devotion, O Nārada. / And we two sons of Dharma, named Nara and Nārāyaṇa— / 97
I merged into Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet, and the younger one became Phālguna. / Brahmā, Īśa, Śeṣa, and Dharma stood together right there. / 98
In the meantime, the gods beheld an excellent chariot, / wrought of pure gold, with varied seats and furnishings, / 99

text_mt:
[Durgā,] seated upon the back of a lion and accompanied by her two sons, gladly / descended swiftly from the chariot and bowed to Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
Along with her two sons, that goddess of fair countenance sat down. / Gaṇeśa and Kārttikeya, having bowed to Kṛṣṇa, who is beyond the highest,
bowed to Śaṅkara, to Dharma, to Ananta, and to the lotus-born [Brahmā]. / Seeing those two lords of the gods, the gods nearby stood up.
The gods gave their blessings and seated them beside them; / filled with joy, the gods conversed pleasantly with them.
The gods remained within the assembly before Lord Hari, / and the cowherds and milkmaids were filled with wonder in many ways.
Kṛṣṇa, whose lotus face was smiling, said to Kamalā [Lakṣmī]: / "Go to the house of Bhīṣmaka, endowed with various jewels,
and take birth, eternal goddess, in the womb of the queen of Vidarbha. / Going to Kuṇḍina, O virtuous lady, I shall take your hand [in marriage]."
Seeing Pārvatī, those goddesses swiftly arose / and seated the sovereign goddess upon a charming, jewelled throne.
O best of brahmins, Pārvatī, Lakṣmī, and the presiding goddess of speech [Sarasvatī] / sat there upon a single seat, having exchanged appropriate greetings.
The cowherd maidens also spoke to them with affection; / some milkmaids spoke with joy in their presence.
There Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of the universe, said to Pārvatī: / "O goddess, in the form of a portion, in the auspicious Vraja of Nanda,
take birth, O auspicious Mahāmāyā, bringer of creation and dissolution, / in the womb of Yaśodā through the seed of Nanda.
Village by village across the earth, I will cause worship to be offered to you, / throughout the entire earth with devotion, in cities and in forests.
There humans, filled with joy, shall worship you as the presiding goddess / with various divine articles and offerings.

Upon merely seeing Kaṃsa, you will depart to the side of Śiva. / Having relieved the earth’s burden, I shall return to my own abode."
Having spoken thus, Śrī Hari swiftly addressed the six-faced [Kārttikeya]: / "My child, you shall go to the earth in the form of a portion.
Take birth in the womb of Jāmbavatī, O lord of the gods. / Let all the gods go to the earth in their portions.
I shall certainly remove the burden of the earth." / Having spoken thus, the Lord of Rādhikā remained upon his excellent throne.
The gods and goddesses, cowherds and milkmaids remained, O Nārada. / At that moment, Brahmā stood up before Hari
and, joining his hands, humbly spoke to the beloved of the universe:
Brahmā said:
"Attend, O all-pervading Lord, to the petition of your servant!
Give the command, O highly fortunate one: whose place on earth shall be where? / The master is always the protector, the savior, and the lord of his servants.
He is the servant and the eternal devotee who carries out the Lord's command. / Which gods with what form, and which goddesses with which part,
and where is each to have their domain and purpose on the earth?" / Hearing the words of Brahmā, the Lord of the universe replied:
"Where each has their proper place, that I shall explain in accordance with the rule."
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
"Kāmadeva shall be the son of Rukmiṇī, and the virtuous Rati shall be Māyāvatī,
who dwelt in the house of Śambara in the form of a shadow. / You [Brahmā] shall be his son, named Aniruddha.
Bhāratī [Sarasvatī] shall be the daughter of Bāṇa in the city of Śoṇitapura. / Ananta, the Lord of the universe, [shall appear] from the womb of Devakī as the son of Rohiṇī;
because of his extraction from the womb through divine illusion, the lord shall be named Saṃkarṣaṇa. / Kālindī is the daughter of the sun, and on earth [she appears] as a portion of Gaṅgā.
Tulasī [shall appear] as a half-portion, and Lakṣmaṇā is a princess.

text_mt:
Sāvitrī, the mother of the Vedas, shall be the virtuous lady named Nāgnajitī.
Vasundharā [shall be] Satyabhāmā, and the goddess Sarasvatī shall be Śaibyā. / Rohiṇī and Mitravindā shall be princesses.
Ratnamālā, the wife of the sun, shall be born from a part of the Lord of the universe, / and Suśīlā from a portion of Svāhā. Rukmiṇī and the others make nine wives;
from a half-portion of Durgā comes Jāmbavatī—these are remembered as the ten principal queens. / Let the daughter of the mountain [Durgā] go to the house of Jāmbavat with a half-portion.
Long ago in Kailāsa, an instruction came from Śaṅkara to Pārvatī / [concerning] Viṣṇu, dweller in Śvetadvīpa, who had come to Kailāsa: / 'Embrace him, my beloved; there is no fault by my command.'"
Brahmā said:
"How did that instruction of Śiva come to the goddess, O Lord of Rādhikā, / previously concerning conversation with Viṣṇu, who dwells in Śvetadvīpa?"
The Blessed Lord said:
"Long ago, all the gods went to see Gaṇeśa. / Viṣṇu himself went from Śvetadvīpa to the abode of Śaṅkara.
Having seen Gaṇeśa, he sat down rejoicing upon a comfortable seat. / With delight, everyone beheld his form that enchants the three worlds:
wearing a diadem and earrings, clad in an excellent yellow garment, / lovely, dark in complexion, endowed with fresh youth,
anointed with sandalwood, agallochum, musk, and liquid saffron, / adorned with the splendour of jewelled ornaments, his lotus face smiling,
seated upon a jewelled throne and surrounded by his attendants, / saluted by all the gods, worshipped and praised by Śiva.
Seeing that Viṣṇu, Pārvatī, with a joyful face and eyes, / covered her face with her garment out of modesty, O virtuous lady.
Looking again and again at that exceedingly handsome form, / the chaste lady, covering her face, gazed without blinking,
smiling, with a sideways glance at that supremely wondrous form; / plunged into an ocean of bliss, her hair stood on end.
For a moment she looked at the five-faced, white-complexioned, three-eyed [Śiva]...
holding a trident and an iron bludgeon, handsome as tens of millions of Kamas. / For an instant she saw him dark-hued, with one face and two eyes, / with four arms, clad in yellow garments, adorned with a garland of forest flowers. / Whether established as one Brahman with distinction of forms or without distinction, / seeing him, she became filled with desire through Viṣṇu's māyā. / 'The three gods, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara, are my portions; / and through superior excellence over the other two, he who is made of the quality of sattva is supreme.' / Seeing him with devotion, her body bristling with horripilation, / Pārvatī worshipped the Paramātman, the Lord, in her mind. / And Śaṅkara himself understood Durgā's inner intention, / being the inner self of all, the Blessed Lord, the Inner Ruler, the master of the universe. / Calling Durgā into solitude, Hara spoke to her himself; / he instructed her in various ways, with beneficial, true, and unassailable words. / Śrī Śaṅkara said: / Hear my petition, O daughter of the mountain: / give erotic delight to Hari, the Paramātman; may it be well with you! / I, Brahmā, and Viṣṇu are the one eternal Brahman; / being one without division, he possesses diversity of forms according to functions. / You are the one Prakṛti, the mother of all, having all forms; / you are speech in Svayambhū; you are Lakṣmī on Nārāyaṇa's chest; / you are Durgā upon my chest. Understand the spiritual truth, O virtuous woman! / Having heard Śiva's words, the queen of the gods said to him: / Pārvatī said: / O friend of the poor, O ocean of compassion, why is there no compassion from you toward me? / You, the lord of the worlds, were obtained by me after long penance as my husband. / O lord, you ought not to abandon a handmaid such as me! / Speak not, speak not such unfitting words, O Maheśvara! / I will certainly obey your command, O Mahādeva: / having obtained birth in another body, I shall worship Hari, O Hara! / Having heard these words, Maheśvara fell silent.
